newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Metlife sees gains in platinum shares.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Metlife sees gains in platinum shares.

text.p: Platinum mining shares have not fully reacted to the improvement in the metal's price and could show further gains, Metropolitan Life resources fund manager Chris Visser said on Wednesday.

Visser said a strategic emphasis on platinum had helped his fund win the top ranking in the Pretoria Graduate School of Management's report on mining and resources funds for the six months to June 30.
"Platinum has finally broken its link with gold and has helped to counter the bad performance of the yellow metal.
"Traditionally, the platinum price closely follows gold price movements. Different forces are now driving the markets of these two precious metals," he said.
The platinum price tracked gold until the third week of May, when platinum broke away towards $500 while gold continued to slide.
Platinum was bid late on Wednesday at $405 while gold was sought at $319.90 to $320.00.
Visser said he would continue to limit his exposure to gold, but believed there were further gains to made on platinum.
He said the paper and pulp sectors continued to offer promise.
